lessons.title: A club formed from two Cologne sides
lessons.subtitle: The merger of two local teams created a club that quickly shaped German football.

story.title: Two clubs become one
story.body: Kölner BC 01 and SpVgg Sülz 07 joined forces after the Second World War. Their merger gave Cologne a new club with ambitions beyond the city leagues.

story.title: A new national champion
story.body: The unified side became a major force in the early Bundesliga era. Within its first two decades, Köln had won the German championship and the new national league.

facts.label: Formation date
facts.prompt: On what date did Kölner BC 01 and SpVgg Sülz 07 merge to form 1. FC Köln?
facts.scope: The club's founding through the merger
facts.evidence: The club history gives the merger date as Friday, 13 February 1948.

facts.label: Founding clubs
facts.prompt: Which two clubs merged to create 1. FC Köln in 1948?
facts.evidence: The official club history names Kölner BC 01 and SpVgg Sülz 07 as the merger partners.

facts.label: First German title
facts.prompt: In which year did the newly formed 1. FC Köln first win the German championship?
facts.evidence: The club history identifies 1962 as Köln's first German championship.

lessons.title: Seven seasons in royal blue
lessons.subtitle: Farfan joined Schalke from PSV in 2008 and remained with the club until 2015.

story.title: A move from Eindhoven
story.body: Farfan transferred from PSV Eindhoven to Schalke in the summer of 2008. He became an important wide attacker during seven seasons in Gelsenkirchen.

story.title: A new chapter abroad
story.body: In 2015 he left Schalke for Al-Jazira. His spell included domestic trophies and a run to the Champions League semi-final.

facts.label: Schalke arrival
facts.prompt: In which year did Jefferson Farfan transfer from PSV Eindhoven to Schalke?
facts.evidence: Schalke's farewell page says he arrived from PSV in summer 2008.

facts.label: Previous club
facts.prompt: Which Dutch club did Farfan leave to join Schalke?
facts.evidence: The Schalke article identifies PSV as his previous club.

facts.label: Departure year
facts.prompt: In which year did Farfan leave Schalke for Al-Jazira?
facts.evidence: Schalke's farewell article says he left for Al-Jazira in summer 2015.

lessons.title: A decisive brace against Valencia
lessons.subtitle: Farfan scored twice in Schalke’s 3–1 Champions League win over Valencia in March 2011.

story.title: A tie still in balance
story.body: Valencia and Schalke entered their Champions League round-of-16 second leg level at 1–1 on aggregate. Farfan helped break the tie with two goals.

story.title: A late clincher
story.body: Schalke won the match 3–1 and advanced 4–2 on aggregate. Farfan’s second goal arrived in added time.

facts.label: Second-leg date
facts.prompt: On what date did Farfan score twice against Valencia in the Champions League?
facts.evidence: UEFA's report dates Schalke's 3–1 second-leg win to 9 March 2011.

facts.label: Farfan goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Farfan score in Schalke’s second-leg win over Valencia?
facts.scope: Farfan's scoring in the 9 March 2011 match
facts.evidence: UEFA's match report credits Farfan with two goals.

facts.label: Aggregate result
facts.prompt: What was the aggregate score when Schalke eliminated Valencia in 2011?
facts.evidence: UEFA reports Schalke advanced 4–2 on aggregate.

lessons.title: A long run ends in a winner
lessons.subtitle: Farfan scored late at Leverkusen to give Schalke a 1–0 away victory in October 2011.

story.title: A difficult away match
story.body: Schalke visited Bayer Leverkusen in the Bundesliga on 23 October 2011. The match remained scoreless until the closing minutes.

story.title: Farfan breaks through
story.body: Farfan scored in the 82nd minute to settle the match 1–0. Schalke’s own match archive calls attention to his long solo run for the winner.

facts.label: Match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Farfan score the winning goal away to Bayer Leverkusen?
facts.evidence: Schalke's 2011/12 archive dates the away match to 23 October 2011.

facts.label: Winning goal minute
facts.prompt: In which minute did Farfan score Schalke’s winner at Leverkusen?
facts.scope: Farfan's winning goal in the October 2011 league match
facts.evidence: The club match record lists Farfan's goal at 82 minutes.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the final score when Farfan’s late goal beat Leverkusen?
facts.evidence: Schalke's match archive records a 1–0 away victory.

lessons.title: A Bundesliga career as creator and scorer
lessons.subtitle: Farfan’s Schalke league totals show both his goals and his role in creating chances.

story.title: A long league run
story.body: Farfan played 170 Bundesliga matches for Schalke and scored 39 goals. He also created goals for teammates, recording 49 assists in the league.

story.title: A broad contribution
story.body: Those numbers describe his Bundesliga record for Schalke. They exclude his DFB-Pokal and European matches, where he also contributed.

facts.label: Bundesliga appearances
facts.prompt: How many Bundesliga appearances did Farfan make for Schalke?
facts.evidence: Schalke's farewell article records 170 league matches for the club.

facts.label: Bundesliga goals
facts.prompt: How many Bundesliga goals did Farfan score for Schalke?
facts.evidence: The club states he scored 39 goals in his 170 Bundesliga appearances.

facts.label: Bundesliga assists
facts.prompt: How many Bundesliga assists did Farfan provide for Schalke?
facts.evidence: Schalke's farewell report records 49 league assists.

lessons.title: A return to the Rhineland
lessons.subtitle: Modeste’s second Cologne spell followed his first major Bundesliga scoring season at the club.

story.title: A striker returns
story.body: Modeste first joined Köln in 2015 after playing for Hoffenheim. After a spell in China, he returned to the club and again became a central part of the attack.

story.title: A prolific campaign
story.body: His 2016/17 league season brought 25 Bundesliga goals for Köln. That scoring run helped the club qualify for European competition.

facts.label: First Köln spell began
facts.prompt: In which year did Anthony Modeste begin his first spell with 1. FC Köln?
facts.evidence: The DFB player record lists his Köln club spell as beginning in 2015.

facts.label: Previous Bundesliga club
facts.prompt: Which Bundesliga club did Modeste leave before joining Köln in 2015?
facts.evidence: The DFB profile lists Hoffenheim immediately before his first Köln spell.

facts.label: Return to Köln
facts.prompt: In which year did Modeste return to Köln after his time in China?
facts.evidence: The directly readable 2018/19 Köln roster lists Anthony Modeste with an entry date of 17 November 2018.

lessons.title: A hat-trick against Hamburg
lessons.subtitle: Modeste scored three times in Köln’s 3–0 home win in October 2016.

story.title: A game opened up late
story.body: Köln faced Hamburg in the Bundesliga on 30 October 2016. Modeste scored the opener, then struck twice more in the final half-hour.

story.title: Three goals, three points
story.body: His hat-trick produced a 3–0 win. It was one of the standout performances in his productive 2016/17 season.

facts.label: Match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Modeste score a hat-trick against Hamburg in the Bundesliga?
facts.evidence: The match record dates Köln's 3–0 victory to 30 October 2016.

facts.label: Goals in the match
facts.prompt: How many goals did Modeste score in Köln’s 3–0 win over Hamburg?
facts.scope: Modeste's scoring in the 30 October 2016 match
facts.evidence: The match record lists all three Köln goals for Modeste at 61, 82 and 86 minutes.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the final score of Köln’s Bundesliga match against Hamburg on 30 October 2016?
facts.evidence: The match report records Köln winning 3–0.

lessons.title: The goal that lifted Köln toward Europe
lessons.subtitle: Modeste’s goal against Bremen helped turn a tense 2017 match into a defining win.

story.title: A season-changing match
story.body: Köln hosted Werder Bremen in May 2017, knowing a win would strengthen its push for European qualification. Modeste scored after the break to give his team a two-goal cushion.

story.title: A city celebrates
story.body: Köln held on and won 4–3. The club later remembered the evening as a turning point on the road back to European competition.

facts.label: Match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Modeste score against Werder Bremen in Köln’s 4–3 win?
facts.evidence: The club's retrospective places the memorable Bremen match on 5 May 2017.

facts.label: Modeste’s goal
facts.prompt: In which minute did Modeste score Köln’s 4–2 goal against Bremen?
facts.scope: Modeste's second-half goal against Werder Bremen
facts.evidence: The club account says Modeste scored shortly after halftime to make it 4–2.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the final score of Köln’s May 2017 home match against Werder Bremen?
facts.evidence: The club's match retrospective records a 4–3 Köln win.

lessons.title: Twenty-five league goals
lessons.subtitle: Modeste’s 2016/17 Bundesliga scoring total placed him among the league’s top finishers.

story.title: A high-scoring league season
story.body: Modeste scored 25 Bundesliga goals for Köln in 2016/17. The total describes league matches only, not every competition.

story.title: A title in another division
story.body: DFB also lists Modeste as a 2018/19 2. Bundesliga champion. That second-division honour belongs to a later campaign than his 25-goal top-flight season.

facts.label: Bundesliga goals
facts.prompt: How many Bundesliga goals did Modeste score for Köln in the 2016/17 league season?
facts.evidence: The Bundesliga matchday page explicitly says he netted 25 goals for Cologne in the 2016/17 campaign.

facts.label: League appearances
facts.prompt: How many Bundesliga appearances did Modeste make for Köln during the 2016/17 season?
facts.evidence: The DFB Datencenter season record lists 34 Bundesliga appearances for Köln in 2016/17.

facts.label: Later league honour
facts.prompt: Which league championship does DFB list for Anthony Modeste in 2018/19?
facts.evidence: The DFB profile directly lists Meister 2. Bundesliga: 2018/2019 in its personal honours section.

lessons.title: The 1978 double
lessons.subtitle: A league title and a cup triumph made 1977/78 Köln’s most successful season.

story.title: Two trophies in one campaign
story.body: Köln collected both of Germany’s major domestic prizes in 1977/78. The club later described it as its most successful season.

story.title: The cup came first
story.body: On 15 April 1978, Köln beat Fortuna Düsseldorf in the DFB-Pokal final. The win was part of a campaign that ended with the league championship as well.

facts.label: Double season
facts.prompt: Which season brought 1. FC Köln both the Bundesliga championship and the DFB-Pokal?
facts.evidence: The club history calls 1977/78 its most successful season and records both the league and cup title.

facts.label: Cup-final opponent
facts.prompt: Which opponent did Köln defeat in the 15 April 1978 DFB-Pokal final?
facts.evidence: The club's anniversary report says Köln beat Fortuna Düsseldorf in the final.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the score when Köln beat Fortuna Düsseldorf in that 1978 cup final?
facts.evidence: The club report records a 2–0 victory, with goals in the 71st and 90th minutes.

lessons.title: A cup final against the city rival
lessons.subtitle: Köln’s latest major trophy came in a 1983 final against Fortuna Köln.

story.title: A derby on the national stage
story.body: The two Cologne clubs met in the 1983 DFB-Pokal final. Pierre Littbarski broke the deadlock in a tight match.

story.title: One goal settled it
story.body: The 1–0 result gave Köln the cup. The club still lists that win as its most recent title.

facts.label: Final date
facts.prompt: On what date did Köln defeat Fortuna Köln in the DFB-Pokal final?
facts.evidence: The DFB match record dates the final to 11 June 1983.

facts.label: Final result
facts.prompt: What was the final score of Köln’s 1983 DFB-Pokal win over Fortuna Köln?
facts.evidence: The DFB match report records a 1–0 Köln victory.

facts.label: Winning goal
facts.prompt: Who scored Köln’s winning goal, and in which minute of the 1983 final?
distractors: Roger van Gool in the 90th minute
facts.scope: The deciding goal in the 1983 final
facts.evidence: The DFB match timeline credits Pierre Littbarski with the only goal at 68 minutes.

lessons.title: A teenager steps into the first team
lessons.subtitle: Podolski made his senior breakthrough in Cologne before his first Bundesliga goal arrived weeks later.

story.title: A local talent gets his chance
story.body: Podolski made his Bundesliga debut as an 18-year-old in November 2003. He came into a side that was struggling, but his first-team opportunity quickly became a regular role.

story.title: Goals in the first season
story.body: His debut campaign brought ten league goals in 19 appearances. His first Bundesliga goal came away to Hansa Rostock, three weeks after his debut.

facts.label: Bundesliga debut
facts.prompt: On what date did Lukas Podolski make his Bundesliga debut for Köln?
facts.evidence: Köln's retrospective states that Podolski debuted against Hamburg on 22 November 2003.

facts.label: Age at debut
facts.prompt: How old was Podolski when he made that Bundesliga debut against Hamburg?
facts.evidence: The club describes the debutant as 18 years old.

facts.label: First-season scoring
facts.prompt: How many Bundesliga goals did Podolski score in 19 appearances during his first top-flight season?
facts.evidence: Köln's retrospective gives his first-season return as ten goals in 19 matches.

lessons.title: Four goals in Cottbus
lessons.subtitle: Podolski scored four times in Köln’s five-goal away win in January 2005.

story.title: A remarkable afternoon
story.body: Köln visited Energie Cottbus in the second division on 23 January 2005. Podolski supplied four goals in a match that finished 5–3.

story.title: Promotion push
story.body: The four-goal display came during the campaign in which Podolski became the 2. Bundesliga’s leading scorer and helped Köln earn promotion.

facts.label: Match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Podolski score four goals against Energie Cottbus?
facts.evidence: The club's Podolski retrospective dates the 5–3 Cottbus match to 23 January 2005.

facts.label: Personal goal total
facts.prompt: How many of Köln’s five goals did Podolski score in the 5–3 win at Cottbus?
facts.scope: Podolski's scoring in the 23 January 2005 match
facts.evidence: The club retrospective says Podolski scored four of Köln's five goals.

facts.label: Competition
facts.prompt: In which competition did Podolski score four times at Cottbus in January 2005?
facts.evidence: The club's season account identifies the game as a second-division match.

lessons.title: A late lob against Freiburg
lessons.subtitle: Podolski settled a goalless home match with an 88th-minute finish in 2011.

story.title: The game stays level
story.body: Köln and Freiburg were still scoreless late in their February 2011 Bundesliga meeting. Podolski found a way through with a lob in the closing minutes.

story.title: A winner in the 88th
story.body: His finish made the final score 1–0. The goal became one of the signature moments of his second spell at Köln.

facts.label: Match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Podolski score his late winner against Freiburg?
facts.evidence: The club retrospective dates the Freiburg home win to 26 February 2011.

facts.label: Goal minute
facts.prompt: In which minute did Podolski score the winning lob against Freiburg?
facts.evidence: The club's account identifies the lob as an 88th-minute goal.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the final score when Podolski’s 88th-minute goal beat Freiburg?
facts.evidence: The club retrospective records a 1–0 Köln win.

lessons.title: A Köln career in numbers
lessons.subtitle: Two spells in Cologne shaped Podolski’s club record and his route into the German national team.

story.title: A lasting connection
story.body: Across his two spells at Köln, Podolski played 181 competitive matches and scored 86 times. His club career included both his first-team emergence and his return from Bayern.

story.title: From Köln to Germany
story.body: Podolski earned 69 senior Germany appearances while he was a Köln player. He later finished his international career with 130 caps and 49 goals.

facts.label: Köln appearances
facts.prompt: How many competitive appearances did Podolski make across his two spells with 1. FC Köln?
facts.evidence: The club's career retrospective reports 181 matches for Köln.

facts.label: Köln goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Podolski score in competitive matches for Köln?
facts.evidence: The club's retrospective lists 86 goals in his 181 Köln matches.

facts.label: Germany caps as a Köln player
facts.prompt: How many senior Germany appearances had Podolski made while playing for Köln?
facts.scope: Germany appearances during Podolski's Köln playing periods
facts.evidence: The club's DFB-debutants feature says he had made 69 Germany appearances as a Köln player.

lessons.title: From Westfalia to Schalke 04
lessons.subtitle: A Gelsenkirchen football club formed in 1904 and adopted the name it still carries two decades later.

story.title: A miners’ district club
story.body: The club began in the Schalke district of Gelsenkirchen in 1904, under the name Westfalia Schalke. Its identity grew alongside the industrial community around it.

story.title: A lasting name
story.body: In 1924 it became FC Schalke 04. The club went on to win seven German championships, the last in 1958.

facts.label: Founding year
facts.prompt: In which year was the club that became FC Schalke 04 founded as Westfalia Schalke?
facts.evidence: The club milestones page dates its foundation to 1904 as Westfalia Schalke.

facts.label: Name change
facts.prompt: In which year did Westfalia Schalke adopt the name FC Schalke 04?
facts.evidence: The official timeline identifies 1924 as the renaming year.

facts.label: Last German championship
facts.prompt: In which year did Schalke win its seventh and most recent German championship?
facts.evidence: Schalke's milestones page dates its seventh and last German championship to 1958.

lessons.title: Schalke wins in Milan
lessons.subtitle: A 1997 UEFA Cup final went to extra time and penalties before Schalke lifted its first European trophy.

story.title: A narrow lead travels to Italy
story.body: Schalke beat Inter 1–0 in the first leg of the 1997 UEFA Cup final. Inter levelled the tie in Milan, sending the final into extra time.

story.title: The shoot-out decides it
story.body: Schalke held its nerve from the spot and won 4–1 on penalties. Marc Wilmots converted the decisive kick.

facts.label: First-leg scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored Schalke’s 70th-minute goal in the first leg of the 1997 UEFA Cup final?
facts.evidence: UEFA's final history credits Marc Wilmots with Schalke's 70th-minute first-leg goal.

facts.label: Aggregate score
facts.prompt: What was the aggregate score after Inter equalised the 1997 final in Milan?
facts.scope: Two-legged 1997 UEFA Cup final before penalties
facts.evidence: UEFA records one 1–0 win for each side, making the aggregate 1–1.

facts.label: Penalty shoot-out
facts.prompt: What was Schalke’s score in the penalty shoot-out that decided the 1997 UEFA Cup final?
facts.evidence: UEFA's official final history says Schalke won the shoot-out 4–1.

lessons.title: A cup semi-final with twelve goals
lessons.subtitle: Schalke and Bayern drew 6–6 after extra time in a 1984 DFB-Pokal semi-final.

story.title: A scoreline keeps changing
story.body: On 2 May 1984, Schalke and Bayern traded goals in a remarkable DFB-Pokal semi-final. The match remained level after extra time.

story.title: A first meeting was not enough
story.body: Under the rules then in force, the teams replayed the semi-final. Bayern won the replay 3–2, so the 6–6 draw did not send Schalke through.

facts.label: Semi-final date
facts.prompt: On what date did Schalke and Bayern draw 6–6 after extra time in the DFB-Pokal?
facts.evidence: The DFB Datencenter dates the 6–6 semi-final to Wednesday, 2 May 1984.

facts.label: Score after extra time
facts.prompt: What was the score after extra time in Schalke’s first 1984 cup semi-final against Bayern?
facts.evidence: The DFB record gives the result as 6:6 after extra time.

facts.label: Replay result
facts.prompt: Who won the replay of the 1984 DFB-Pokal semi-final, and by what score?
facts.evidence: The DFB retrospective explains the tie went to a replay, which Bayern won 3–2.

lessons.title: A Dutch striker arrives in Gelsenkirchen
lessons.subtitle: Huntelaar joined Schalke from AC Milan in 2010 and returned to the club in 2021.

story.title: A move from Milan
story.body: Huntelaar transferred from AC Milan to Schalke in August 2010. The move began a long first spell with the Royal Blues.

story.title: A return years later
story.body: After leaving in 2017, the Dutch striker returned to Schalke in January 2021 for a second spell.

facts.label: Arrival year
facts.prompt: In which year did Huntelaar transfer from AC Milan to Schalke?
facts.evidence: Schalke's farewell retrospective says he moved from AC Milan in August 2010.

facts.label: Previous club
facts.prompt: Which club did Huntelaar leave to join Schalke in 2010?
facts.evidence: The club identifies AC Milan as the club he left for Schalke.

facts.label: Return year
facts.prompt: In which year did Huntelaar return to Schalke for a second spell?
facts.evidence: The Schalke transfer profile records his return in January 2021.

lessons.title: Two goals in the cup final
lessons.subtitle: Huntelaar scored twice as Schalke defeated Duisburg to win the 2011 DFB-Pokal.

story.title: An early lead
story.body: Schalke faced MSV Duisburg in the 2011 cup final in Berlin. Huntelaar scored the second goal in the first half and added another after the break.

story.title: A five-goal final
story.body: Schalke won 5–0 and lifted the cup. Huntelaar’s brace was a major part of the emphatic win.

facts.label: Final date
facts.prompt: On what date did Huntelaar score twice in Schalke’s DFB-Pokal final against Duisburg?
facts.evidence: Schalke's match archive dates the final to 21 May 2011.

facts.label: Final goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Huntelaar score in Schalke’s 5–0 cup-final win over Duisburg?
facts.evidence: Schalke's archive credits him with goals in the 22nd and 70th minutes.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the score when Schalke beat Duisburg in the 2011 DFB-Pokal final?
facts.evidence: The official archive records a 5–0 Schalke win.

lessons.title: A record-equalling scoring season
lessons.subtitle: Huntelaar topped the Bundesliga scoring chart with 29 goals in 2011/12.

story.title: The league’s leading scorer
story.body: Huntelaar scored 29 Bundesliga goals in 2011/12, more than any other player in the division.

story.title: A Schalke benchmark
story.body: That total equalled Klaus Fischer’s club record for league goals in a single season, set in 1975/76.

facts.label: League goals
facts.prompt: How many Bundesliga goals did Huntelaar score in 2011/12?
facts.evidence: Schalke says Huntelaar won the scoring title with 29 league goals.

facts.label: Scoring-table finish
facts.prompt: Where did Huntelaar finish among Bundesliga scorers in 2011/12?
facts.evidence: The Bundesliga's season guide names Huntelaar as the 2011/12 league top scorer.

facts.label: Previous record-holder
facts.prompt: Whose Schalke single-season Bundesliga goal record did Huntelaar equal with 29 goals?
facts.evidence: The club says his 29 goals equalled Klaus Fischer's 1975/76 record.

lessons.title: A prolific European scorer
lessons.subtitle: Huntelaar’s European scoring record was exceptional even within his prolific Schalke career.

story.title: Goals beyond the league
story.body: Huntelaar scored 31 times in 49 Champions League and Europa League appearances for Schalke.

story.title: A club benchmark
story.body: The club identifies him as its record scorer in European competition, with a clear lead over the next Schalke player on its list.

facts.label: European appearances
facts.prompt: How many Champions League and Europa League appearances did Huntelaar make for Schalke?
facts.evidence: Schalke's farewell article reports 49 appearances in the Champions League and Europa League.

facts.label: European goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Huntelaar score in UEFA club competitions for Schalke?
facts.scope: Huntelaar's Champions League and Europa League matches for Schalke
facts.evidence: Schalke reports 31 goals in those 49 European appearances.

facts.label: Schalke European record
facts.prompt: What scoring distinction did Schalke assign Huntelaar in European club competitions?
facts.evidence: The club calls him its record scorer in European competition.
